record.what_it_does: The WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API) lets businesses programmatically send and receive WhatsApp messages, manage message templates, phone numbers, groups, and calls, and receive delivery/incoming-message events via webhooks.
record.auth_notes: Meta's docs describe the underlying token model as OAuth-style access tokens ('Authentication uses OAuth (not 2.0) access tokens'). For a multi-tenant agent toolkit, Embedded Signup (an OAuth flow) is used to obtain access on behalf of a customer's WhatsApp Business Account; day-to-day API calls then use a long-lived System User access token sent as an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. There is also an official MCP layer that itself uses 'OAuth-based authentication with Read and Manage scopes.'
record.access_notes: Anyone can create a Meta app, get a free test WhatsApp Business Account/phone number, and send test messages immediately with no payment method. But calling the API on behalf of WABAs you don't own (the scenario for a multi-user agent toolkit) requires the `whatsapp_business_messaging`/`whatsapp_business_management` permissions at Advanced Access, which requires Business Verification and Meta App Review.
record.main_blocker: Business Verification + Meta App Review (Advanced Access) required to message WABAs outside the developer's own business
